Topic: Impact on Patient Access to Services

Clues (max 200 words): 
- "Sometime we come for a whole day no, patient will come."
- "They say if they come they will be told that they have the virus."
- "Patients were afraid to come. They say 'I don’t want to go and be told that I have corona.'"
- "Even free health care patients were not coming, let alone those not covered by the free health care."
- "It is only now that they have started coming."
- "Most of them refuse to come to clinic."
- "The only thing is that when you meet the criteria or you are suspected, you will not be treated till you do the test."

Reasoning (max 150 words): 
The clues reveal a severe decline in patient access to healthcare services due to fears surrounding COVID-19. Many patients avoided seeking care, leading to days with no patients at all and significant anxiety about being diagnosed with the virus. This avoidance extended even to those eligible for free healthcare, indicating a widespread reluctance to engage with the system. Furthermore, the implementation of strict criteria for treatment added barriers to access, compounding the issue. The eventual return of patients suggests a gradual recovery, but the initial impact was profound, severely affecting healthcare delivery.

- "When it started our MS is somebody who is experience in that. He put everything in place."
- "We take triage we have an isolation side to observe patient before they take the patient in."
- "We properly check patients, them to put up their mask."
- "Even visitors are checked before entering."
- "Now when you come, in the morning you are first sent to the triage for proper checking before you enter."
- "The only thing is that when you meet the criteria or you are suspected, you will not be treated till you do the test."

Reasoning (max 150 words): 
The clues demonstrate a well-structured response from the healthcare facility to the COVID-19 pandemic. Key measures included establishing triage and isolation protocols, ensuring proper patient checks, and enforcing mask-wearing policies. The organized management of both patients and visitors reflects a commitment to safety and infection control. However, the requirement for patients to meet certain criteria before receiving treatment highlights a cautious approach that may delay care for urgent needs. This comprehensive response showcases the facility's adaptation to the challenges posed by the pandemic while striving to maintain operational integrity.

- "This is a dry, dry one."
- "I don’t know of any support."
- "Whenever we come to work, we will just say hi to one another."

The lack of support for mental health further exacerbated feelings of anxiety and stress. The mention of a "dry" environment suggests a stark and challenging workplace atmosphere. Together, these clues underscore the significant impact of the pandemic on staff morale and mental health, emphasizing the need for supportive measures in healthcare settings.

Topic: Comparison of COVID-19 Response to Ebola

Clues (max 200 words): 
- "Any way I think they did well this time compare to the Ebola."
- "During the Ebola, people were saying Ebola is not real."
- "But this time, covid, people tried."
- "The health people try but we the ordinary people were stubborn that was why we were affected so much."
- "The health sector responded well this time."

Reasoning (max 150 words): 
The clues provide a comparative view of public and healthcare sector responses to COVID-19 versus Ebola. The respondent notes that the health sector’s response to COVID-19 was more effective, with greater community compliance and acknowledgment of the disease's seriousness. This contrasts sharply with the skepticism encountered during the Ebola outbreak. The improvement in public perception and response reflects lessons learned from past experiences, indicating an evolution in health communication and community engagement strategies. This comparison highlights the importance of public cooperation in managing health crises effectively.

- "the 20% of the patients that used to come are no longer coming."
- "Because we just have to utilize light, we will put on the generator."
- "The hospital was running under loss."
- "Most often people are under oxygen, so there should be twenty-four hours light."

Reasoning (max 150 words): 
These clues reveal the financial hardships faced by the healthcare facility during the pandemic. A significant drop in patient numbers has led to reduced revenue, exacerbated by increased operating costs associated with maintaining essential services such as power for oxygen machines. The facility's inability to cover its expenses has resulted in financial losses, highlighting a critical concern for healthcare sustainability during crises. The reliance on generators for power further adds to the financial strain, indicating the urgent need for support mechanisms to ensure the viability of healthcare services in challenging times.

- "We spend more than what we receive."
- "Most often people are under oxygen, so there should be twenty-four hours light."
- "The hospital was running under loss."
